A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe RealGeneral, with reliably matchable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither includes an appendix; supplementary material referenced in the text is not present in either supplied PDF.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original image-generation evaluations, qualitative examples and component/attention-mask ablations, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original benchmark results, generated examples and ablation findings reported in v1.

M1.justification: The CogVideoX1.5 two-frame formulation, Unified Conditional Embedding, three-branch SC-AdaLN, FCD attention mask and task-specific LoRA remain unchanged. Section 3 revisions are editorial.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training datasets, DreamBench and COCO2017 evaluations, and subject-driven, canny-to-image and depth-to-image tasks. Figure 1 also retains the same additional task demonstrations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–7. Table 2 retains ControlNet with SD1.5 and FLUX, OmniGen and OminiControl. Newly cited RealCustom works are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same sample counts, 512×512 resolution, metrics, subject segmentation, training budget and inference settings. Both use 20 DreamBench images and 20 prompts, 5,000 COCO2017 validation images, 4,000 training iterations and 50 denoising steps.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 retain identical component-removal and attention-mask ablations. The base-model analysis in Section 4.3/Figure 7 and qualitative comparisons are also unchanged; no additional robustness or error analyses appear.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and qualitative examples are retained. For example, RealGeneral's customization CLIP-I/DINO/CLIP-T scores remain 0.849/0.668/0.314, and its canny FID/SSIM remain 17.50/0.44 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same denoising objective, embedding operations, AdaLN formulation and masked attention. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same temporal in-context-learning proposal, task-agnostic principles and efficiency claims. The claimed 14.5% subject-similarity and 10% canny-quality improvements are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning cross-modal interference, video pretraining and ablation effects are unchanged. Future-work qualifications about foundation-model quality and replacing task-specific LoRA with a fully integrated framework are also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit GitHub repository link alongside a revised project-page link. Implementation settings and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. This improves code-location documentation, although repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 newly cites DSE-GAN, RealCustom and RealCustom++, and expands Section 2.1's discussion of task-specific controllability. Section 2.3 shortens the PixWizard and UniReal descriptions while preserving the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, condenses the UniReal comparison, revises author/corresponding-author text and adds a funding acknowledgment. The section order and central narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is refreshed at higher resolution with the same examples, and Figure 3 moves from PDF page 5 to page 4. Captions, front matter and reference layout receive limited adjustments; table structures and other figure content are preserved.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the explicit repository pointer and expanded customization-related discussion modestly improve resource discovery and context. Copyediting and the sharper overview figure improve presentation. The method, experimental evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
